text:
Priya (AE): @Anya @Mike looping you in to kick off the Pendo MLOps POC. Customer wants a two-week technical POC to validate infra, quality, and costs. Quick agenda below, please flag gaps. :wave:

Anya (SE): Thanks. Can we confirm scope: transformer-based summarization + rerank for internal docs? Also need to know if they require private deployment (VPC) or hosted API.

Priya (AE): Yes — primary use case is high-quality summaries for internal compliance docs, secondary is query reranking. Customer is leaning hosted but demands SOC2, data residency in EU, and optional VPC if we need to land logs.

Mike (Eng): For the two-week POC we should run:
- baseline hosted inference against their 500 sample docs
- dedicated config test (small Dedicated pool) if they request throughput SLA
- compare quantized model vs full fp16 for cost/latency

Jordan (Security): Quick security checklist from our side: SSO/SAML, KMS for keying, audit logs, PCI/PHI scope clarifications, and data retention policy. Also need their security questionnaire (NDA already signed?).

Lee (Customer PM): NDA is signed. We can share a short security pack but their infosec will still push the standard questionnaire. Timeline: they want results and a decision in 3 weeks. Can the POC be compressed to 10 business days?

Anya (SE): 10 business days is tight but doable if we scope evals tightly. Proposed milestones:
Day 0: Kickoff + data ingestion prep
Day 1-3: Baseline hosted runs + metrics collection
Day 4-6: Dedicated config + perf tuning (batching, KV cache)
Day 7-8: Eval runs (500 prompts), quality analysis, hallucination checks
Day 9: Wrap + delivery of report and cost estimates

Priya (AE): Success criteria (customer side) they agreed to in call:
- Summaries meet 'sufficient' label match >= 85% on curated eval prompts
- Hallucination rate < 5% on sampled outputs
- 99th percentile latency < 1s for summary (for doc sizes ~2k tokens) or fallback path
- Estimated hosted cost <= $0.12 per 1k tokens (they asked for a ballpark)

Mike (Eng): Minor note: 1s p99 for 2k tokens is aggressive on some GPU profiles. We should propose p95 < 400ms, p99 < 1.2s as realistic for medium-sized instances. Also include fallback model variant in routing policy.

Jordan (Security): For the questionnaire, ask them to prioritize the following fields so we can prefill: data flows, third-party subprocessors, key management, retention window, incident response contact. If they insist on on-prem, route to Private deployment team.

Anya (SE): Sample eval prompt we plan to run (short list):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the following compliance report focusing on obligations and next steps:"
Document sample: <their doc snippet>
Metrics: ROUGE-L, factuality check, ctrl hallucination count, human acceptability (binary)
```

Priya (AE): Pricing Q&A from customer: are committed Dedicated discounts available for a two-week POC? They want committed cost modeling for a 6-12 month ramp after POC.

Mike (Eng): For short POC we can offer hosted usage credits and a short-term Dedicated trial (no annual commit). For 6–12 month modeling we'll produce a capacity estimate and committed price tiers (SE/Q for numbers).

Priya (AE): Action items:
- @Anya: Send detailed POC runbook + sample eval prompts to Lee today (owner) — due EOD.
- @Mike: Prepare rough perf/cost estimate for hosted vs small Dedicated pool — due tomorrow noon.
- @Jordan: Draft a one-pager on security artifacts we can provide (SOC2, KMS options, audit logs) — due +48h.
- @Lee: Share 500 sample docs and their security questionnaire link — due EOD tomorrow.

Anya (SE): I'll include example ingestion scripts and a small test harness. Will also add quick instructions for turning on KV caching and batching flags.

railbot: Scheduled: "POC-kickoff-reminder" in 24 hours for channel attendees.

Lee (Customer PM): Thanks all — I'll upload the sample set and the questionnaire by EOD tomorrow. 10-business-day timeline works from our side if infra is ready. :thumbsup:

Priya (AE): Great. I'll send calendar invite for kickoff + include agenda. If anyone sees a blocker (EU data residency, KMS integration, or legal redlines) call it out here ASAP.

Mike (Eng): One potential blocker: if they require HSM-backed key storage in EU-only region, private deployment may be required — flagging as dependent on Jordan's review.

Jordan (Security): Acknowledged. I'll queue the questionnaire and aim to have preliminary answers in 48 hours.

Priya (AE): Closing note: goal is a concise report at end of week with clear go/no-go and recommended next steps. Thanks team!
